claims.text: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) is a leading Indian shipyard engaged in constructing, repairing, and modernizing warships and submarines for the Indian Navy.

cites.quote: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (“MDL” or “the Company”), a Navratna Defence Public Sector Undertaking under the administrative control of the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, is India’s leading shipyard engaged in the construction, repair, refit, modernisation and lifecycle support of warships, submarines and allied engineering products.

claims.text: MDL has developed significant expertise in warship construction, submarine building, and systems integration, supporting India's maritime defense capabilities.

cites.quote: Over the decades, the Company has developed significant expertise in warship construction, submarine building, systems integration, engineering, project management and lifecycle support services.

claims.text: The company is strategically positioned to leverage opportunities in defense shipbuilding, commercial shipbuilding, and ship repair due to India's focus on naval modernization and maritime capability enhancement.

cites.quote: India’s continuing focus on naval modernisation and maritime capability enhancement presents substantial long-term opportunities for warship construction, submarine programmes and lifecycle support services.

claims.text: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited reported a revenue of 1,300,631 lakh for FY26, with a PAT margin of 19.8%.
The company achieved a revenue CAGR of 22.7% from FY22 to FY26, growing from 573,328 lakh to 1,300,631 lakh.
PAT CAGR for the same period was 44.8%, indicating strong profitability growth.
Revenue for Q2 FY27 was 294,270 lakh, a decrease of 45.4% YoY, indicating a significant decline in performance.
PAT for Q2 FY27 was 34,640 lakh, down 53.8% YoY, reflecting a substantial drop in profitability.
The company experienced a deceleration in revenue growth from Q1 FY27 to Q2 FY27, with a 57.5 percentage point decrease.
Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited has a net worth of 884,316 lakh, indicating a strong equity base.
The company has not engaged in any public or preferential issue of shares, mergers, or foreign collaborations during the audit period.

cites.quote: the audit period there were no instances of: (i) Public / Right / Preferential Issue of Shares / Debentures / Sweat Equity etc.; (ii) Redemption / Buy-Back of securities; (iii) Merger / Amalgamation / Reconstruction, etc.; (iv) Foreign Technical Collaborations;

claims.text: In FY26, the CFO to PAT ratio was -103%, indicating negative cash flow from operations despite profitability.
Free cash flow for FY26 was -312,569 lakh, reflecting significant cash outflows exceeding operational cash inflows.
The company had a positive CFO to PAT ratio of 87% in FY25, showing better cash conversion in the previous year.
In Q2 FY25, management expected to maintain revenue levels without a fall, but Q2 FY27 revenue fell by 45.4% YoY, contradicting this expectation.
Management anticipated a 50% revenue increase over two years from Q2 FY26, but Q2 FY27 results are not yet reported to confirm this.
Management expected higher margins from submarine contracts in Q2 FY26, but Q2 FY27 EBITDA margins are not reported to confirm this.

scorecard_takeaways.text: In Q2 FY25, management promised a 10-12% revenue growth for FY25, delivering 20.8%, exceeding the low end by 10.8 percentage points.
In Q2 FY26, management anticipated FY26 revenue of approximately INR 12,500 crores with 5% growth, delivering 13.8%, exceeding the low end by 8.8 percentage points.
Management's guidance on capex and margins in FY26 was not measurable as actual figures were not reported in quarterly results.
